The organization, the project, the figures and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are asked to fix the HR self-service portal at Linwood Retail, a fictional retailer. It launched last month; store staff aren't using it and HR calls doubled.
handover: Store staff have no work computers; the portal needs a company login.
howItWorks: The desk shows the ticket queue against the priority matrix and each service's status.
Move on a day at a time. A decision comes to you at each service review; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

usage.label: Look at portal usage and HR call data
usage.available: not busy and phase == "run" and isNull(usageAt)
usage.why: Done, or finish what you are doing first.

effects.log: Look at portal usage and HR call data.

effects.finding: Head-office staff use it; store staff don't; HR calls doubled from stores.

stores.label: Talk to store staff and managers

stores.why: Done, or finish what you are doing first.

effects.log: Talk to store staff and managers.

effects.finding: Staff were never trained, have no device at work, and the HR team still expects paper forms from stores.

options.label: A four-dimension analysis, external factors assessed, and a relaunch addressing every dimension

source.note: How long each task takes and when each review or event arrives are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

then.log: Day 2: managers are told to enforce use; staff complain to the union and calls rise further.
Day 3: a staff complaint about access to pay data reaches the regulator.
Day 4: usage in stores stays near zero and HR calls stay doubled.

choices.label: Analyze all four: organizations and people (no training, HR still on paper), value streams and processes (paper flow unchanged), partners (none), information and technology (fine, but no device access)

effects.log: The analysis names the people and process gaps.

choices.feedback: A service needs all four dimensions together; here people and processes were neglected.

choices.label: Look for technical defects
choices.feedback: There's no technical fault to find.

pestlePrompt.title: Outside factors
pestlePrompt.context: A new law requires pay data to be accessible to all staff; many store staff have no smartphone allowance.

choices.label: Assess the legal duty (equal access), economic (no device allowance) and social factors, and plan shared store kiosks plus mobile access
choices.feedback: External (PESTLE) factors act on every dimension and must shape the design.

choices.label: Make it mobile-only
choices.feedback: Excludes staff without smartphones, against the access duty.

choices.label: Ignore the access law for now
choices.feedback: Staff without access can't see their pay data as the law requires.

relaunchPrompt.title: Relaunching
relaunchPrompt.context: The sponsor wants it relaunched next week.

choices.label: Relaunch store by store with training, kiosks, HR's process switched off paper, and a partner for kiosk support
choices.feedback: Considering the dimensions together turns a working system into a working service.

choices.label: Run training only
choices.feedback: Staff still have no device and HR still uses paper.

choices.label: Relaunch the same way with an email

reflection.question: Write the relaunch record for the HR director.

parts.label: Why it failed
parts.criteria: People and processes neglected; external factors.
parts.modelAnswer: The technology worked, but store staff had no training or device and HR's paper process didn't change; the access law and no device allowance mattered too.

parts.label: Relaunch
parts.criteria: Training, kiosks, process change and a kiosk partner, store by store.
parts.modelAnswer: We relaunch store by store with training, shared kiosks, HR off paper, and a partner supporting kiosks.

scoring.modelReasoning: A product or service succeeds only when all four dimensions are considered together: organizations and people, information and technology, partners and suppliers, value streams and processes. External political, economic, social, technological, legal and environmental factors act on each dimension and shape the design.
